newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end higher on BOJ's move.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end higher on BOJ's move.

text.p: April 16 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.13 99.09

Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Wednesday's TIFFE day session higher after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) unexpectedly refrained from its regular 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) money market operation, indicating an accommodative stance.
Gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures also provided support.
December's day session turnover was 56,000 lots.
Money traders had expected the central bank to take either a neutral or slightly accommodative stance on Wednesday by draining 100 billion or 200 billion yen.
The market was in surplus by about 200 billion yen going into the day.
"The December rose following the BOJ's accommodative stance. It rose as high as 99.14 in the afternoon after the benchmark June JGB futures briefly rose above 127.00," said a brokerage house trader.
Key June JGB futures ended up 0.20 at 126.76, after rising as high as 127.02.

Traders said the bulk of buying was short-covering rather than setting up of new long positions. The December's upside was still heavy, as there were sell orders of about 30,000 lots from 99.14 to 99.16, they said.
Some swap-related buying may also have been partly responsible for gains in euroyen futures, traders said.
Some swap players were receiving shorter-term interest rates while paying longer-term rates in a move which appeared to be an unwinding of curve-flattening trades, traders said.
Some players' bids in euroyen futures may be linked to these swap plays, they said.
The three-year interest rate swap (IRS) rate was quoted at 1.20/1.24 percent, down from 1.25/1.29 percent late on Tuesday.

In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at around 0.44 percent in the morning, but rose to around 0.47 percent in the afternoon. Tuesday's weighted average of the unsecured call rate was 0.42 percent.

"The BOJ may have taken an accommodative stance to make sure that the overnight rate will remain stable at below 0.5 percent from the start of the new bank reserve reporting period," said a trust bank trader.
The new one-month reserve reporting period started today.

Asked about Wednesday morning's accommodative stance, a BOJ official told Reuters: "The BOJ simply conducted its operation after seeing money market conditions." About 210 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.55 percent and another 15 billion yen worth at 0.54 percent. Three-month CDs were issued at 0.55 percent on Tuesday.
One-month CDs were offered at 0.52 percent, down from 0.53 percent on Tuesday. Two-month CDs were offered at 0.53 percent, also down from 0.54 percent in the previous session.
-- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
